title: Prefix prefetch + fallthrough routing workshop notes
body:
Objective:
This workshop walks customer-facing engineers through a hands-on lab for implementing prefix prefetch combined with fallthrough routing across model variants. Goal is a repeatable kit to show 20-60% token cost reductions on common chat workloads while keeping 95th-p latency within SLOs via graceful fallbacks.

Context and motivation:
- Many customers see long-tail tokens from repeated prompt prefixes (system messages, instructions, user histories).
- Redwood runtime supports KV caching and prefix-level prefetch, but cache hit strategies and routing policies are often tuned ad-hoc.
- This lab demonstrates a reproducible approach: 1) detect stable prefixes; 2) warm a prefetch KV entry; 3) route initial requests to a higher-throughput variant; 4) on cache miss or quality regression, fall through to a higher-fidelity model.

Prereqs (local laptop + Redwood sandbox):
- Access to Redwood sandbox account with experimental models (token: REDWOOD-EXAMPLE-XXXX)
- k8s local cluster (kind/minikube) or Redwood dev stack running
- Python 3.11, curl, jq
- ~2GB sample chat logs (see linked_artifacts)

Lab setup steps:
1) Prepare sample workload:
   - Extract stable prefixes from sample chat logs: run `python tools/prefix_extract.py --input sample_chats.jsonl --min-count 5 --out prefixes.txt`.
2) Create two model variants on the sandbox: `fast-quant` (int8, aggressive batching) and `high-fidelity` (fp16).
   - Console: Models -> New Variant -> copy bases and set quantization profile
   - CLI example: `redwood models create-variant --base gptx-1 --name fast-quant --quant int8`
3) Implement a prefetch orchestrator (sample code below). The orchestrator watches incoming requests, matches against `prefixes.txt`, and fires a warm prefetch call for the cached KV for the target model.

Sample orchestrator (minimal Python):

# --- begin sample code ---
import requests, json, time
REDWOOD="https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1"
TOKEN="REDACTED"
HEADERS={"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

def prefetch(model, prefix):
    payload={"model": model, "input": prefix, "prefetch": True}
    r=requests.post(f"{REDWOOD}/generate", headers=HEADERS, json=payload, timeout=5)
    return r.status_code==200

if __name__=="__main__":
    with open('prefixes.txt') as f:
        prefixes=[l.strip() for l in f if l.strip()]
    for p in prefixes[:20]:
        ok=prefetch('fast-quant', p)
        print('prefetch', 'ok' if ok else 'fail', p[:60])
        time.sleep(0.12)
# --- end sample code ---

Routing policy sketch:
- Default route: fast-quant with low cost and high batching
- If prefetch reported cache warm and response score >= quality_threshold -> keep route
- If response score < quality_threshold OR cache miss flagged -> immediate synchronous fallback to high-fidelity variant and record metric
- Maintain per-customer routing table in Redis: {customer: variant, last_warm_ts, miss_count}

Experiment matrix to run during workshop:
- Baseline: route all to high-fidelity, measure tokens and p95 latency (30k requests).
- Prefetch-only: prefetch fast-quant but route to high-fidelity unless prefetch success (measure delta).
- Full strategy: route to fast-quant by default; fallback on miss/regression.
Measure: token cost, p50/p95 latency, quality regression rate (human or automated eval set).

Observability and telemetry hooks:
- Instrument prefetch success/fail, route decisions, fallback events as spans/tags in tracing system.
- Expose dashboard panels: prefetch hit rate, fallback rate, latency distribution per-variant, cost per-1000 requests.
- Add alert if fallback rate > 5% for 1 hour.

Troubleshooting notes and gotchas:
- Cold start noise: initial prefetches will show higher latency; warm for 10-20 minutes before measuring.
- Over-aggressive prefetch can waste tokens for low-frequency prefixes — tune min-count threshold.
- Quantized variant may hallucinate slightly different phrasing; use eval set to detect regressions by BLEU/ROUGE or embedding-similarity.

Customer-facing demo script (10–15 min):
1) Show baseline metrics for sample app (latency/cost).
2) Enable prefetch orchestrator and show logs of warm events.
3) Toggle routing policy to fast-quant and demonstrate a fallback on an intentionally adversarial prompt.
4) Summarize expected economics: projected per-month savings given X qps.

Follow-ups and extension ideas:
- Auto-tune prefetch rate using feedback loop from fallback metrics.
- Tiered routing: add a mid-tier variant (quant4 + safety filters) for partial fallbacks.
- Integrate with Redwood Optimize recommendations to decide quant/ batch knobs per-route.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Curl prefetch example:
  curl -s -X POST "https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"fast-quant","input":"<prefix>","prefetch":true}' | jq .

- Quick check for cache warm metric (CLI):
  redwood metrics query --name prefetch_hit_rate --window 1h --group-by variant

Reference artifacts and tickets:
- CONF-1234-prefetch-design (design sketch)
- GH-PR-5122 (orchestrator prototype)
- jira/SE-WORKSHOP-77 (workshop logistics)

Notes to facilitators:
- Keep the lab light on infra: provide a preconfigured Docker image with the orchestrator and sample prefixes to avoid yaw in setup time.
- Encourage participants to pick one metric to optimize (cost or latency).
- Capture customer-specific prefixes during discovery session to show immediate improvement within the workshop timebox.

Unresolved questions:
- Default quality threshold for fallback: start 0.92 embedding-similarity vs baseline — need cross-customer calibration.
- Autoscaling interplay: prefetch traffic can create short-lived bursts; ensure Dedicated pools have burst capacity or fallbacks are region-aware.

End of workshop notes.
